Update: Having looked more into the system at Mixplate's request, it actually doesn't look as bad as I initially thought. Original reply below for posterity.

--

It's cool that he's built this but sending his kid to school plugged into it is fucking terrifying and (imo, as someone who does this stuff for a day job) hideously irresponsible.

Let us be clear: If ANYTHING happens to jam that pump into 'on' mode, that kid will die and it will be the father's fault.

There's a reason that medical devices are so expensive. It's because they have to go through tons of testing, design reviews, more testing, long term trials, etc. etc. This isn't because 'big pharma' wants to make more money, it's because we really really don't want people trusting their life to a device until we're reasonably sure it's not going to kill them.

A breadboarded-together device is not reliable enough to send to school in a kid's backpack. It could get too hot, be hit by a flying soccer ball, be shaken around, get wires twisted together and shorted out... there are a million ways for it to fail in a fatal manner. And an insulin overdose is fatal if not caught in time.

Seriously no. It's about as safe as strapping your kid into a big quadcopter and flying them around the place. Sure it seems cool but it's not worth the risk.
